A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedCoG study. The main text and complete appendices are readable, including equations, figures, tables, prompts, and case studies, and retained material can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MedCoG benchmark evaluations, component ablations, threshold studies, and memory-evolution results, including Tables 2, 8, and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds monitor precision/recall/F1 measurements and calibration comparisons in Tables 3 and 8.

M1.justification: The regulator, five-strategy pool, SCoT, KG retrieval, memory procedures, and four prompt listings are retained. Equation (1)'s correction matches the routing behavior already described in v1; it does not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MedQA-Full and the same five hard subsets: MedQA, MedMCQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, and PubMedQA. The added diagnostics reuse existing coverage; Figure 1's broader aggregation introduces no new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The ten main baselines in Section 4.2 and Table 2 are unchanged. Appendix H/Table 8 adds median- and quartile-based threshold policies as evaluated alternatives to held-out calibration, providing limited new comparisons within MedCoG.

E3.justification: v2 adds oracle-referenced monitor precision/recall/F1 evaluation across seven backbones, including Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-Max, and five calibration settings. Appendices F–G introduce alternative efficiency measures, reference choices, and curve fits. Figure 1 changes from MedQA to aggregation across five hard sets; the original benchmark sample counts and implementation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation through direct monitor-quality assessment, efficiency-metric comparisons, scaling-curve sensitivity, and calibration stability analyses. These examine central routing and efficiency assumptions beyond v1's retained threshold sweeps, component ablations, memory-domain comparisons, and case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, experimental confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new median/quartile thresholds are calibration alternatives, not uncertainty estimates; no additional run counts or random-seed information are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains all accuracies but revises IIE values, including MedCoG-META from 0.443 to 0.438 and MedPrompt from -3.000 to -0.208. Figure 1 replaces the MedQA analysis (5.5× density, R²=0.91) with five-hard-set analysis (6.2×, R²=0.996), so this is not a same-setting gain. Tables 3, 7, and 8 add substantial monitor, efficiency, and calibration results.

T1.justification: Equation (1) replaces the zero-shot condition Ic ∧ If ∧ Ik = 0 with Ic + If + Ik = 0. This corrects the formal rule to require all three binary indicators to be zero, consistent with the existing prose. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central framework and contributions remain intact. The abstract and introduction revise the headline inference-density claim from 5.5× to 6.2× under Figure 1's changed aggregation and qualify mitigation of scaling laws as mitigation of diminishing returns.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking model capacity to monitoring reliability, explains the CoT reference for IIE, discusses fitting-function limitations, and attributes Qwen3-8B's calibration exception to underestimated scores. The pilot discussion softens sufficient medical-reasoning capacity to high potential; the existing domain and knowledge-coverage limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page project-page link and documents the new calibration controls in Appendix H. Model versions, temperature, ranker, retrieval settings, case-bank construction, hardware disclosure, and prompt listings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 and the bibliography add dParallel, Ada-R1, and Snell et al.'s test-time compute scaling work to contextualize inference efficiency. The related-work taxonomy and principal novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology and prose revisions, expands metric explanations, inserts Appendices F–H and acknowledgements, and updates author/publication information. The overall narrative and existing appendix content remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replotted with revised axes and caption for five-hard-set results, and Tables 3, 7, and 8 are added. Figure 3 moves columns and existing material reflows and renumbers; Figures 2–6 retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: The added monitor diagnostics and calibration comparisons strengthen examination of the central regulation mechanism, while Equation (1) now correctly formalizes the described gate. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Appendix F claims the highest Zero-Shot-referenced IIE despite Table 7 showing CoT at 1.487 versus MedCoG-META at 0.595. Table 3 also reports GPT-4o knowledge F1=0.80 with precision 0.59 and recall 0.95, an unexplained inconsistency under the standard F1 formula.
